scope: Synthetic Bennington town; not a medical or epidemiological model. US surveys use different ages and recall windows; rates below guide variety, not individual diagnosis. Narrative intensity is a separate design choice.

sources.note: ACS 2020–2024: 6,358 households, 2.25 persons per household, median household income $59,446, poverty 13.2%, median gross rent $1,133; town, not county or CDP.
Historical household composition is a calibration reference, not a current exact count. New synthetic towns target about one third one-person households, with single-parent and shared homes.
US population estimates include differing survey years; conditions overlap. Anxiety, depression, PTSD, OCD, bipolar disorder, personality conditions, ADHD and eating disorders have separate pages.
Emotion-regulation difficulties and treatment; the label does not imply abusive behavior or criminality.
2024 NSDUH, ages 12+: 16.8% past-year substance-use disorder, 9.7% alcohol-use disorder. These are overlapping conditions, not rates of daily use. Treatment receipt is much lower than need.
Sports, arts, cultural/affinity, volunteer/academic and special-interest organizations inspire fictional game schedules.
Local senior programming includes walking, painting, games and social support, often free or low-cost.
PERMA as separable building blocks, not a diagnostic happiness score.
Autonomy, competence and relatedness; distinguish intrinsic aims from externally controlled status pursuits.
Turning toward, away and against bids for connection; describe observable behavior, not deterministic divorce forecasts.
Brown, Sokal and Friedman: the proposed universal critical positivity ratio is unfounded. Counts are descriptive, never a magic flourishing threshold.
Capitalization and active constructive responding: evidence concerns response patterns, not fixed personality types or guaranteed outcomes.
Treatment depends on individual difficulties and evidence; CBT is one approach, and care does not equal instant cure.
